The RESA Project investigates whether rural settlements in Mato Grosso can be economically viable while keeping the forest standing. It covers the state's three biomes (Amazon, Cerrado and Pantanal) and draws on an analysis of its 141 municipalities and three pilot areas.

```{r}
atalhos_inicio()
```

## Mato Grosso in figures

The cards below summarise indicators of family farming, settlements, emissions and deforestation in Mato Grosso, giving the source, unit and year of each figure.

```{r}
kpis_inicio()
```

::: {.nota-fonte}
This page uses the official series from PRODES, the satellite-based deforestation monitoring system run by the National Institute for Space Research (INPE). The official series replaces the one used earlier in project materials, as the correction note in [Emissions and deforestation](resultados/emissoes.qmd) explains. The totals shown are official state totals and may differ slightly from the municipal sum (see [Data](dados/index.qmd)).
:::

## Distribution of the 141 municipalities by type and biome

The maps below show the municipal type of family farming, as defined in the project's Manuscript 1, and the dominant biome of each municipality. A dark outline marks the host municipalities of the three pilot areas. Hover over a municipality (or tap it) to see its name, and click it to open its profile.

```{r}
mapas_inicio(altura = 380)
```

## What's new

**6 November 2026 — Version 0.1.5.** The Observatory is now also published from the project's GitHub account, and the recommended citation on the [About](sobre.qmd#como-citar) page now gives that address. The results are unchanged.

**6 November 2026 — Version 0.1.4.** Aligned the [Municipal typology of family farming](resultados/tipologia.qmd) page with the current version of Manuscript 1, with no change to the numerical results. The page now states the two hypotheses, explains that they were fixed after an exploratory analysis of the same data and declares that Hypothesis 1 is not supported in the form stated. The oblimin and promax rotations now have the same standing, and caveats on Hypothesis 2, suppression and the silhouette have been added. On the [Agricultural Census tenure data and agrarian reform](resultados/posse.qmd) page, corrected the reference to "low" tenure in the T3 label.

**5 November 2026 — Version 0.1.3.** Corrected the ranks of tied municipalities in the ranking charts, which now match those on the profiles and cards, and the wording of the area card on this page, which refers to the area of establishments rather than of the state.

**5 November 2026 — Version 0.1.2.** Added an English version of the website, available via the flags in the menu bar, and listed the project team in [About](sobre.qmd).

**23 October 2026 — Version 0.1.1.** Revised the page text to use scientific language, with no change to figures, sources or results.

**19 October 2026 — Version 0.1.** First version for the project team, covering:

- the 141 municipalities, with `r nrow(IND)` indicators and IBGE symbols displayed;
- the indicator sources: 2017 Agricultural Census data on family farming, INCRA/SIPRA, SEEG 13 and the 2006–2017 dynamics;
- the municipal typology from Manuscript 1 (k = 5, provisional labels);
- Census tenure data and agrarian reform;
- emissions and deforestation by type, with the official PRODES series and the correction note;
- the three pilot areas, with identifying details only, and the six specific objectives;
- the literature, limited to metadata, with 115 references on carbon, markets and ESG and 38 studies compared for SO4;
- the data for download, with a data dictionary, sources and licences.
